title: New Media: The Industry
summary: ## Transition to new media in India

The first news websites were launched by media houses around 1986 but were replicas of the print editions and only created awareness about the media houses. The actual transition happened after 1996 when several independent media houses brought out news websites; after 2000 most independent media organisations and their websites closed down, and convergence became popular.

Independent media houses were funded by venture capitalists: big businessmen who lend money to people who want to start a business, expecting to get back several times what they invest. They saw new media as a possible business option and as a way to access political groups and to earn through internet transactions. But Indian customers prefer to buy after seeing the product ('look and feel'), so most ventures closed. Media practitioners learnt that new media needed innovative revenue models and that content must be sold.

Print media played a major role in the freedom struggle and ruled for two decades after independence; television appeared in the seventies and cable television changed newspapers' designs and forms of writing. With new media, technology became an important criterion (earlier creativity was the primary skill). Debates: will the media turn digital (like television, new media takes time to stabilise, and will not throw out print or television) and creativity versus technical skills (technology is useful only if it supports creativity). A more effective form of communication does not destroy the earlier form. Convergence means that several media forms such as print, radio, television and new media exist and co-exist simultaneously, with media organisations running print, television, radio and new media divisions together under one roof.

Customisation of news: a user registers on a news website and gets only the news of interest, e.g. cricket scores on a mobile. A website is the standard new media product: corporate websites give initial information to customers and employees ('contact us' section) and may invite blogs for feedback; social networking sites let anyone become a member and trace friends; online libraries serve research and academics; online learning (e-learning) is education through the internet; online buying and selling sites; online games, graphics, animations, cartoons, photography sites and blogs.

objective: Fill in the blanks: Customization of news means whatever kind of news interests you will be ______ to you; new media news stories are kept ______ and crisp.
State true or false: (a) Customization of news means whatever kind of news interests you will be sent to you. (b) News stories for new media are kept very short and crisp.
Fill in the blanks: The ______ of the urban and rural divide is a significant feature of language press growth; new media stories are broken into ______ stories.
Fill in the blanks: Convergence means the coming together of ______, ______ and ______.
State true or false: (i) Early web editions were replicas of print editions. (ii) New media will throw out print and television.
vsa: Give any two examples of new media.
Websites and blogs (also social networking sites, online libraries, e-learning).
What do you understand by media convergence?
The coming together of several media forms such as print, radio, television and new media, which co-exist and are run under one roof.
Define venture capitalist and give one example.
A big businessman who lends money to people who want to start a business expecting high returns; e.g. businessmen who funded the new media ventures after 1996.
List any two examples of new media platforms where people can connect and interact with others.
Social networking sites and blogs (also websites with forums).
Explain any two functions of a website.
It gives initial information to customers and employees through a 'contact us' section, allows feedback through blogs, and offers online services such as shopping and news.
sa: What is a website? Write any two features of a website.
A website is the standard new media product, a set of web pages of an organisation or person; features: contact us section with phone and e-mail, news and blogs for feedback, online services.
Discuss how new media technologies have opened service-based business avenues. Give examples.
New media ventures need little infrastructure and earn through advertising, subscriptions and services such as e-learning, online tickets booking and tourism packages.
Explain the transition to new media in India.

News websites began around 1986 as replicas; the real transition came after 1996 when independent houses started websites funded by venture capitalists; after 2000 most closed and convergence became popular.
la: Discuss the impact of new media in India.

Venture capital funded new media but Indian customers' 'look and feel' preference closed many; practitioners learnt innovative revenue models; technology joined creativity as a criterion and media forms converged.
Write an essay on how convergence is changing the face of the Indian media industry.
Print, television, radio and new media co-exist; organisations run all divisions under one roof, earlier forms change for the better rather than disappear, and creativity is combined with technology.
